research_rationale:
EO 6925-A (December 19, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) cancels the President's order of December 30, 1933 approving the Code of Fair Competition for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade, acting 'pursuant to the authority vested in me by Article VIII of the Code of Fair Competition for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade, and by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act'. The held text has one long recital (the Administrator's public hearing on cancellation, the National Industrial Recovery Board's report, and the expectation that the trade's operations would then fall under the Trucking and Construction codes) and one operative sentence beginning 'Now, Therefore': the President adopts and approves the Board's report, recommendations and findings 'and do hereby cancel my order approving said Code.' The machine inventory is one clause spanning the whole text including the recital and the signature block; I replaced it with one clause, characters 749 to 1188, the operative sentence (inventory correction recorded). The command is a one-time cancellation exhausted by performance on the order's own date, December 19, 1934; it is not itself a code approval, so the June 14, 1935 repeal is not its end and, because the approval it cancelled had already ended, is not recorded as a later event. The surviving consequence (the approval stands cancelled) is separated from the exhausted command. The earlier order of December 30, 1933 (EO 6543-J) is held as a separate text and is not this claim's subject; this claim records only the cancelling order. Read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6925-canceling-order-approving-code-for-the-cinders-ashes-and-scavenger.txt, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; 1,367 characters).
